trust_decision.summary: In kapt's incremental-cache reader, decide which classes may be instantiated while deserializing the build-dir cache files java-cache.bin and apt-cache.bin: the cached bytes are treated as untrusted data, so ObjectInputStream may only resolve a fixed whitelist of value classes (plus primitive/array descriptors) and anything else must be rejected and the file discarded.

landing_point.why: The fix commit is titled 'KAPT: Deserialize only a handful of classes from KAPT incremental cache'; the summary's 'Kotlin Build Cache' leads to the raw ObjectInputStream.readObject calls on kapt's cache files, and this first read (apt-cache.bin) is the most obvious sink in that file, with the java-cache read ten lines below.

fix_sites.module_kind: compiler-plugin base library (JVM, kapt-base); invoked reflectively by the Gradle kapt worker and by kapt-cli

fix_sites.entry_point: same JavaClassCacheManager constructor, also reached by the K2 kapt compiler plugin: FirKaptAnalysisHandlerExtension.kt:115 -> KaptContext.init
both public drivers above (the changed line only forwards the KaptLogger for the new warnings)
new private readCacheFromFile helper called from both maybeGetAptCacheFromFile and maybeGetJavaCacheFromFile
new private FilteringObjectInputStream (resolveClass/resolveProxyClass) used by both cache reads

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the fix are about KAPT's processor-side incremental cache (java-cache.bin/apt-cache.bin); the Gradle plugin's classpath snapshot files are a separate, plugin-owned cache written by a different module, so leaving them unfiltered reads as out of the advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same readers must keep round-tripping the legitimate caches written by JavaClassCacheManager.close(): java-cache.bin holds a JavaClassCache with java.net.URI keys and ClassFileStructure/SourceFileStructure values (ClassFileStructure.declaredTypes is a Collections$SingletonSet produced by setOf(...), SourceFileStructure holds LinkedHashSet fields), and apt-cache.bin holds an IncrementalAptCache with java.io.File keys/sets and LinkedHashSet values. A filter tightened by hand from a plain-String reproduction, or one whitelist copied to both files, silently makes every incremental kapt build fall back to a full rebuild.

O6_input_shapes: apt-cache.bin: IncrementalAptCache root object with java.io.File keys/values, LinkedHashSet<String>, HashMap/HashSet wrappers
java-cache.bin: JavaClassCache root object with a custom writeObject emitting a map of java.net.URI -> ClassFileStructure/SourceFileStructure
array class descriptors, including multi-dimensional and primitive arrays ('[', '[L...;'), checked recursively by getNonPrimitiveArrayComponentType
primitive pseudo-type names (int, void, ...), and proxy classes which are rejected outright
a whitelisted-but-wrong root object: expectedClass does not match, so the file is deleted and a fresh empty cache is returned

O7_producer.where: plugins/kapt/kapt-base/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/kapt/base/incremental/cache.kt:169-189 (close() writes both caches with ObjectOutputStream; JavaClassCache's own writeObject is at classStructureCache.kt:74-77)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The Gradle plugin deserializes classpath-entries.bin, ap-classpath-entries.bin and classpath-structure.bin from the very same incApCache directory with a bare ObjectInputStream.readObject
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the plugin's own classpath-snapshot cache, a different feature from the APT incremental cache named in the fix, and it is read from a different module.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module and package: libraries/tools/kotlin-gradle-plugin, org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.internal.kapt.incremental; the same directory is passed as KaptOptions.incrementalCache at KaptWithoutKotlincTask.kt:372 and loaded at KaptTask.kt:226

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ClasspathEntryData.loadFrom deserializes each per-entry structure file ('output.bin' emitted by the @CacheableTransform) with a bare ObjectInputStream.readObject
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Those are Gradle artifact-transform outputs / build-cache entries, not kapt's processor cache, so they look like Gradle's responsibility rather than KAPT's.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the snapshot reader but a different producer: the transform writes output.bin at ClasspathAnalyzer.kt:67 and the snapshot reader calls loadFrom at ClasspathSnapshot.kt:132

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third maybeGet*FromFile for a new kapt cache file (e.g. stub/line-information or processor-option cache) serialized with ObjectOutputStream
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already has two near-identical cache readers/writers and kapt keeps adding incremental state; a maintainer adding a third cache would copy the existing pattern verbatim.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another .bin file placed in the same incApCache directory and read with a bare ObjectInputStream
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This factory already reads three sibling .bin files from that directory and the write path (ClasspathSnapshot.kt:141-158) grows one file at a time as incremental state grows.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap only the two readObject calls in kapt-base cache.kt with a narrow class filter (or ObjectInputFilter) and stop, leaving the Gradle plugin's other .bin readers in the same cache directory untouched and probably breaking legitimate cache round-trips with an over-tight whitelist.
